title: safety-needle-jotter-sylvie-2026
linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE: Trust > SOC2 Prep > Private Deployments (wip)
content:
Quick brain-dump: safety-needle jotter (for myself, messy). Goal: capture the minimum evidence set + open questions for SOC2 mapping specifically around private deployments / customer-managed keys / audit trails. Use this to scope a short checklist for solutions eng + infra handoff.

Context notes:
- Private deployment customers ask for: VPC-lifted control plane, KMS/HSM integration, audit log exports, SSO via SAML/SCIM, and predictable data isolation.
- Type: mostly Type 1 / readiness for Type 2 later. Focus on controls we can demonstrate quickly (config, logs, runbooks).

Top-of-mind risk hypotheses (short):
- R1: Key compromise (customer KMS misconfig/misuse) -> risk to data confidentiality.
- R2: Incomplete audit capture for private clusters (gaps between control plane and runtime logs).
- R3: SSO misconfiguration allows stale accounts to access infra.
- R4: Backup snapshots leaving customer data accessible outside allowed storage.

Minimum evidence we should be able to produce (first pass):
- Config snapshots: sample terraform state + exported topology for one private customer (sanitized).
- KMS integration proof: step-by-step run of customer-initiated key binding + audit of key usage (cloud KMS audit logs).
- Log chain: example pipeline that ships audit logs to customer SIEM + retention policy screenshots (or config).
- SSO/SAML: SCIM provisioning logs + SSO assertion sample (redacted) + disabled-account remediation ticket.
- Runbooks: incident play for key compromise and for failed SCIM sync (dated, owner, last exercised).

Control mapping snippets (raw draft; map to SOC2 criteria later):
- Access Control (AC): SSO enforced for console access + role mappings documented. Evidence: SSO config, role-to-permissions mapping spreadsheet, one deprovisioning ticket.
- System Change (CC): PR review + deploy gating for infra code affecting private deploys. Evidence: PR history, CI job config, approval logs.
- Logging & Monitoring (LM): Centralized audit log ingestion + immutable storage for retention. Evidence: log-export config, storage bucket policy, sample logs with hashes.
- Key Management (KM): Customer-managed KMS integration + periodic key-rotation guidance. Evidence: KMS binding record, rotation schedule, test rotation run.

Open questions / things to chase before formal mapping:
- Q1: Do we have a standard sanitized sample we can give auditors (one-off)? Who owns redaction? (Comms + legal?)
- Q2: Is there a single index of all endpoints that touch customer data in private mode? (I think no.) Need infra to produce an endpoint catalog.
- Q3: For KMS, which cloud providers have complete audit trails available via current instrumentation? (GCP/Azure/AWS differences).
- Q4: Retention windows: what are defaults we expose to customers vs what auditors expect?

Practical next steps (order-of-operations):
1) Spin up a quick "sanitized demo" private deployment and walk through: provisioning -> KMS bind -> SSO integrate -> generate logs. Capture everything as screenshots + exported config. Owner: Ishan. ETA: 1 week.
2) Draft a short runbook for "key compromise" (play + who to call + steps to revoke bindings). Owner: Sylvie (me). ETA: 3 days.
3) Ask infra to produce an endpoint inventory CSV for private deploys. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2 weeks.
4) Identify legal/comms contact for audit sample redaction policy. Owner: Sylvie -> ping Legal.

Evidence quick-check template (to hand to solutions eng):
- Evidence ID (short) | Description | Type (config/log/runbook) | File location | Sanity check (Y/N)
- ex: E-KMS-01 | KMS binding event log | log | s3://private-evidence/demo/e-kms-01.log | Y

Notes to self (random):
- Keep this doc lean; auditors hate irrelevant noise. They want: who, what, when, and how we detect.
- Do not include PII anywhere in exported samples. Redaction rule: remove any raw customer IDs, IPs, and credentials; keep timestamps and event ids.
- For demo evidence, prefer system IDs over names.

Draft wording for an internal email to Solutions Eng / Infra (short):
"Hi SE/Infra — I'm compiling a minimal evidence bundle to accelerate SOC2 mapping for private deployments. Need: one sanitized private deploy export, KMS usage logs, and an endpoint inventory. Can you tag me on the PRs/tickets or drop artifacts into s3://redwood-internal/soc2-wip? I'll coordinate redaction with Legal. Cheers — Sylvie"

Fragmented checklist (to turn into proper ticket list later):
- [ ] Sanitize demo export + upload
- [ ] Confirm KMS audit availability by provider
- [ ] Draft key-compromise runbook
- [ ] Gather SSO provisioning logs + example assertion
- [ ] Produce endpoint inventory CSV
- [ ] Create short mapping doc linking evidence -> SOC2 control IDs

Signature: sylvie — save & iterate.

End of jotter.
